oracles.version: github.com/moby/buildkit v0.33.0 frontend/dockerfile (docker buildx build --print=outline substitute — no Docker daemon in this sandbox)

oracles.status: unavailable: universal-ctags has no parser for this dialect

notes: per-file times exclude the one-time grammar compile (an untimed warm-up extraction precedes timing)
disposition: partial: L1 and L2 are both excellent against a tier-A oracle (buildkit-dockerfile-parser, the same official parser docker buildx build --print=outline uses internally -- no Docker daemon is reachable in this sandbox to run buildx itself) across 3 real subjects/73 files (docker/cli, docker/compose, docker-library/python): sym_recall .9949, sym_precision .9975, ref_recall 1.0, ref_precision 1.0 -- a stage's FROM base (prior stage or external image) is captured unconditionally, matching every other tags dialect's naive same-file call convention. L3 is needs-strategy, for two independent, code-verified reasons, not one query fix: (1) the closed tags-engine import-strategy set (schema/dialect/dialect.cue #ImportStrategy; internal/fusion/resolvestrategy.go's resolveByStrategy switch) has no strategy that maps a FROM's local image tag to the OTHER Dockerfile that built it -- unlike doc-engine cross_file's image-ref (compose.yml declares image+build together; a bare Dockerfile carries no such mapping on its own); (2) even with a strategy, internal/langbench.recompute() never populates xref_precision/xref_recall for kind=="tooling" (its keys list for tooling omits them entirely, and no FamilyXref exists) -- L3 is presently unmeasurable for ANY tool-format dialect, a foundation gap outside one worker's dialects/<id>/ directory (design §2.1's isolation rule), not something to invent around here. COPY --from=<stage> is deliberately not captured either (dialects/dockerfile/tags.scm's header): the grammar keeps every instruction a flat sibling of source_file (a stage's body is a textual run between one FROM and the next, never a subtree under it), so a copy_instruction several instructions after its stage's from_instruction is never contained by it -- attachTSCalls's containment rule would silently drop the capture; modeling that needs a sequential-section scope tree-sitter's query language cannot express, and reworking attachTSCalls is a shared tsextract.go change, again outside this dialect's directory. LB-Q-dockerfile stays unchecked; see LB-Q-dockerfile-rest. Trigger: an Opus-reviewed foundation change adds (a) a tags-engine import strategy for tool-declared local image tags (or an equivalent repo-wide image-tag index a manifest can name) and (b) xref scoring for kind=="tooling" readings in internal/langbench.recompute().
